desc: The single blocker for NVMe file I/O. Linux mounts CJ's exFAT partition off the internal SSD and does real filesystem I/O for ~5 s, then the ANS firmware asserts '[7454]:CQ (Host I/O) DB error, status_reg 0x4, head 63, valid_status 0x4, err_info_0 0x1, err_info_1 0x20000' and the controller dies. m1n1 does equivalent I/O across 3 CQ ring wraps with no complaint. REFUTED SO FAR (all experimentally, transcripts in linux-build-out/): E1 wrap-per-se, E2 batched doorbell, E4 unacked-CQE limit (moved crash head 61->63), E9 IRQ-enabled CQ, E10/E5b concurrency (one usable I/O tag still asserts), E11 non-zero NVMMU TCB slot; plus by code reading: IRQ/poll doorbell race (both take anv->lock), ring/qsize mismatch, IOQ base register ordering, phase-bit convention, posted-vs-nonposted MMIO (m1n1 maps /arm-io nGnRnE too). E6/E7/E8 chased a doorbell-window discrepancy that turned out to be a NON-BUG (stock mmio_nvmmu works; reg[9] from Linux hangs). NINE properties now match m1n1 and it still asserts. REMAINING CANDIDATES: (a) real IRQ-context completion -- Linux completes inside its IRQ handler, m1n1 polls; E9 only set the CQ flag, m1n1 never takes the MSI. This is the strongest lead and needs either a Linux change that defers completion to a thread (sol staged a threaded-IRQ discriminator, ticket 203) or firmware RE; (b) Identify + a live depth-2 admin queue sharing the NVMMU TCB table, which m1n1 never has (ticket 195); (c) CoastGuard fw RE of assert 7454 to decode status_reg/err_info_* and the actual doorbell contract -- the only path that explains rather than eliminates. WRITE SCOPE: CJ authorized writes via the mounted filesystem AND raw writes to p3 only; never raw writes to /dev/nvme0n1 or any APFS partition. IRC 2026-08-02: yuka independently reads APPLE_ANS_UNKNOWN_CTRL as simply ABSENT on 15.x+ firmware (behaving as 14.x without clearing APPLE_ANS_PRP_NULL_CHECK), corroborating the gate we already ship. sven gave the upstream-preferred SHAPE: introduce a new compatible + an apple,firmware-abi property and change behaviour for macOS 15+, NOT firmware-version sniffing -- that supersedes the V_UNKNOWN version-comparison discussion in our drafts. sven also cautions "cdw12 isn't prp": yuka's cdw12=1->0 change and the PRP-null-check are separate, do not conflate. sven recalls the NULL_PRP_PTR_ERR firmware message as what appears without that bit.
